summary: Scope GitHub watch execution identity by event, suppress rollout-only terminal notices and bound execution-detail pages.

replay.detail: No graph projection, replay or repair changes.

schema.detail: No SQL schema or migration changes.

compatibility.detail: GitHub observations add event-scoped workflow execution identity to required_checks facts. Latest suites of the same app/workflow/event supersede older contexts; pre-ready pull-request skips stay pending, while current conditional skips still satisfy checks. Terminal notifications can fire for a new execution on the same head without an observed pending transition. Adding identity to legacy facts alone does not repeat a prior terminal notice. Partial suite/check pages cannot qualify success and expose required_checks.incomplete=true in repository observation facts; no dedicated UI badge is added. Existing watches and commit-status semantics are retained. Execution-detail pages read twenty PRs each instead of one hundred, with the prior 1,000-PR total and 1,000 remembered-identity read bounds retained.

downtime.detail: Selecting this watcher implementation requires the ordinary daemon rollout; restart interruption is unmeasured.

manual.detail: No watch re-registration or CI rerun is required. Curator eligibility still requires its own exact-head review and current check evidence.

recovery.detail: No durable migration is introduced. Rolling back restores the older watcher interpretation and notification limits.
